title: Economic History
description: Original constructed exercises on preindustrial constraints, industrialization, institutions and colonial legacies, labor and demography, monetary and financial history, and historical measurement. Prerequisites: introductory microeconomics and macroeconomics, algebra, ratios and percentages; elementary statistics and causal-inference concepts help with archival and identification items. The course teaches mechanisms and evidence interpretation rather than chronological trivia. Every numerical setting and institutional rule is hypothetical unless explicitly identified otherwise; no contested historical causal explanation is presented as settled consensus. It develops economic history rather than attempting a separate comprehensive history-of-thought survey.
